papers.title: Clinical Reasoning: A 7-Year-Old Boy With Left-Sided Involuntary Movements.
papers.title_zh: 临床推理：一名7岁男孩出现左侧不自主运动。
papers.abstract: Hemichorea is a rare movement disorder that can arise from a diversity of causes. In this case, a 7-year-old boy presented with subacute onset of involuntary movements involving the left upper extremity. This case highlights the importance of careful characterization of abnormal movements in children, as distinguishing chorea from myoclonus, tics, or epileptic automatisms directs subsequent diagnostic testing. It also underscores the broad differential diagnosis of hemichorea in pediatric patients and the need to consider systemic and vascular processes when imaging reveals focal findings. Through stepwise clinical reasoning, this case illustrates how integrating movement phenomenology with neuroimaging and systemic evaluation can uncover an underlying unifying diagnosis.
papers.abstract_zh:
半侧舞蹈症是一种罕见的运动障碍，可能由多种原因引起。在本病例中，一名7岁男孩出现累及左上肢的亚急性发作性不自主运动。该病例凸显了仔细鉴别儿童异常运动的重要性，因为将舞蹈病与肌阵挛、抽动或癫痫性自动症区分开来，有助于指导后续的诊断性检查。它还强调了广泛的差异
儿科患者半侧舞蹈症的鉴别诊断，以及当影像学检查显示局灶性发现时需要考虑全身性和血管性病变。通过逐步的临床推理，本病例阐明了如何将运动现象学与神经影像学和全身性评估相结合，以揭示潜在的统一诊断。

papers.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 功能系统完整性和与不同临床相关因素的整合的互补轴是局灶性癫痫的特征。
papers.abstract: Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation.
papers.abstract_zh:
局灶性癫痫影响分布式脑系统，但对具有临床意义的患者特异性网络组织的表征仍然有限。我们使用静息态功能性MRI估算了重叠的个体化网络，并得出了两个互补的轴：（1）网络对应性，通过规范系统表达来衡量系统完整性；（2）k-枢纽性，通过多网络部分来衡量跨系统整合性。
我们研究了一个术前队列，其中包括305名局灶性癫痫患者和224名健康参与者，以及一个独立的验证队列，其中包括903名患者（涵盖局灶性癫痫、常见全身性癫痫和儿童癫痫综合征）和666名健康参与者。对应关系紊乱在各种局灶性癫痫中普遍存在，而k-枢纽性变化则表现为跨系统整合的侧向化和依赖于综合征的重新分布。
这些轴具有共同的方差，但显示出适度的偏好性关联，其中与认知相关的对应关系与癫痫临床特征的k-枢纽性相关。这些指标共同揭示了个体化脑系统组织中普遍存在且各不相同的变化，将网络拓扑的互补性特征与认知和临床变异联系起来。

papers.title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 人脑类器官揭示了遗传性局灶性癫痫中独立于mTOR过度活化的MGE中间神经元缺陷。
papers.abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

papers.title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels.
papers.title_zh: 胞外塔状结构作为HCN通道中电压传感器-孔耦合的结构枢纽。
papers.abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

papers.title: Rodent studies of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy-induced neonatal seizures: A systematic review on model variations and reporting standards.
papers.title_zh: 缺氧缺血性脑病诱发的新生儿癫痫啮齿类动物研究：关于模型变异和报告标准的系统综述。
papers.abstract: Neonatal seizures resulting from hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) are common and associated with long-term neurological impairment and developmental delays. This clinical burden necessitates better understanding of underlying mechanisms to improve treatment strategies. Rodent models are essential to this field and extensively investigated. However, translating these findings to human patients remains challenging. This review evaluates all preclinical research on rodent models of HIE-induced neonatal seizures to date, assessing model variations, methodological quality, and translational potential. We conducted a systematic search in PubMed and Embase up to March 10, 2025, identifying 134 publications describing 186 HIE induction protocols. Studies exposing rodents to hypoxia at or before postnatal day 21 and presenting unique data on seizure occurrence were included. Results were synthesized narratively. Identified induction protocols comprised three model types: (1) ambient hypoxia, (2) surgically induced ischemia, and (3) ambient hypoxia combined with ischemia. Rat models were most frequently used (67%), and the most common method of HIE induction was ambient hypoxia (63%). Seizures were reported in 88% of model variations, but detection methods, definitions, and monitoring timing varied widely, limiting comparability of seizure outcome data. Potential links between lower age at induction and increased seizure susceptibility and between the combined use of hypoxic/hypercapnic conditions and increased seizure occurrence were observed. Antiseizure medications were inconsistently investigated; phenobarbital showed variable, age-dependent efficacy. Risk of bias, assessed using SYRCLE's risk of bias tool, was generally high. Altogether, this systematic review provides a comprehensive overview of rodent models of HIE-induced neonatal seizures. Although these models have advanced understanding in this field, variability in model design and incomplete reporting limit objective identification of a gold standard model with optimal translatability. Standardization of model parameters, detailed monitoring of behavioral and electrophysiological seizure characteristics, and rigorous reporting practices will enhance reproducibility, optimize laboratory animal use, and strengthen clinical relevance of preclinical findings.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: EEG相关HPO术语对小儿癫痫中表型驱动的变异优先排序的影响。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization.
METHODS: We compiled three HPO-based profiles, differing only in EEG terms: (a) a full profile, including all EEG-specific terms; (b) a profile containing only the non-specific EEG term ("HP:0002353" EEG abnormality); and (c) a profile without any EEG terms.
RESULTS: We identified a total of 185 HPO terms across 33 pediatric patients with epilepsy, with a median of 2 EEG-related terms per patient. Analysis included both phenotypic and gene scoring for each profile. We observed significantly higher scores for the non-specific and no-EEG profiles in both the phenotype and combined Exomiser scores. This effect was also observed in patients whose top gene did not change. The full profile returned the shortest candidate lists, with a median of 82 genes, followed by the no-EEG profile (142 genes) and non-specific EEG (157 genes). The top-ranked gene changed in 24-55% of patients across profile comparisons, while the full-profile top gene remained within the top three in 30/33 (non-specific EEG) and 26/33 (no-EEG) patients.
SIGNIFICANCE: Our study shows that more specific EEG-related HPO terms were associated with lower phenotype and combined Exomiser scores and changed the top-ranked gene in a subset of patients. These findings suggest that EEG-related HPO terms should be curated carefully in phenotype-driven variant prioritization.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: HPO terms are widely used in both clinical and research settings to provide a standardized phenotype description. In this study, we examined how EEG-related HPO terms impact variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. We found that profiles with specific EEG terms were associated with lower phenotype and gene scores compared with those without EEG terms or with non-specific EEG abnormalities. These findings suggest that the choice of EEG-related HPO terms can influence phenotype-driven prioritization results.

方法：我们编制了三个基于HPO的表型，它们仅在EEG术语上有所不同：(a) 一个完整表型，包括所有EEG特异性术语；(b)
)仅包含非特异性EEG术语（“HP:0002353”EEG异常）的表型；以及(c)不包含任何EEG术语的表型。
结果：我们在33名癫痫患儿中总共识别出185个HPO术语，每名患者的EEG相关术语中位数是2个。分析包括对每个特征的表型和基因评分。我们观察到，在表型和组合评分中，非特异性谱和无EEG谱的评分显著更高。
Exomiser评分。在排名第一的基因未发生变化的患者中也观察到了这种效应。完整特征返回的候选基因列表最短，中位数为82个基因，其次是无EEG特征（142个基因）和非特异性EEG特征（157个基因）。在所有特征比较中，24-55%的患者的排名最高的基因发生了变化，而完整特征中排名最高的基因在30/33（非特异性脑电图）和26/33（无脑电图）的患者中仍保持在前三名。
意义：我们的研究表明，更具体的EEG相关HPO术语与较低的表型和Exomiser综合评分相关，并改变了一部分患者中排名最高的基因。这些发现表明，在以表型为导向的变异优先排序中，应谨慎整理与EEG相关的HPO术语。
浅显易懂的摘要：HPO术语在临床和研究环境中均得到广泛使用，以提供标准化的表型描述。

papers.title: Mesial temporal function during language fMRI in pre-surgical epilepsy patients.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫患者术前语言功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）期间的内侧颞叶功能。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Language fMRI paradigms may allow joint assessment of interconnected language and memory function before epilepsy surgery. We characterized activation of a core memory structure, mesial temporal lobe (MTL) during a language fMRI task. We investigated relationships between MTL activation and language and memory performance in individuals with epilepsy.
METHODS: We included 38 left focal epilepsy patients (18 adult, 20 pediatric), and 55 healthy controls (27 adult, 28 pediatric). Participants performed a clinically validated language fMRI task (Auditory Description Decision Task), language, and memory neuropsychological assessments. We computed lateralization index (LI) for bilateral Broca's and Wernicke's language areas and MTL memory regions of Interest (ROIs). We also investigated MTL activation magnitude across participant group (controls, patients), age group (adult, pediatric), MTL side (left, right), and region (anterior/posterior) with a mixed effects model. ANCOVAs assessed relationships between MTL LI or activation magnitude, and language and memory scores.
RESULTS: All groups had left-lateralized MTL activation. We found greater MTL activation magnitude in adult than pediatric patients, and in pediatric controls than patients. Controls had greater anterior, and patients had greater posterior, activation magnitude. Left MTL lateralization was related to language, verbal, and visual memory function in children, and activation strength in left posterior MTL to verbal memory in adults.
SIGNIFICANCE: Our language fMRI task evoked left-lateralized language and MTL activation. Relationships between activation and neuropsychological tests suggest this activation is functionally relevant for evaluation of memory function. Our ADDT task may support both language and memory assessment before epilepsy surgery.

目的：语言fMRI范式可能有助于在癫痫手术前联合评估相互关联的语言和记忆功能。我们对核心记忆结构——颞叶内侧（MTL）在语言fMRI任务中的激活进行了表征。我们研究了癫痫患者的MTL激活与语言和记忆表现之间的关系。
方法：我们纳入了38例左侧局灶性癫痫患者（18例成人，20例儿童）和55例
健康对照组（27名成人，28名儿童）。参与者完成了临床验证的语言fMRI任务（听觉描述决策任务）、语言和记忆神经心理学评估。我们计算了双侧Broca区和Wernicke区以及颞中叶（MTL）记忆感兴趣区（ROI）的偏侧化指数（LI）。我们还研究了不同参与者组（对照组、患者组）、不同年龄组（成人、儿童）的MTL激活幅度。
MTL侧（左、右）和区域（前/后）之间的关系。ANCOVA评估了MTL LI或激活幅度与语言和记忆得分之间的关系。
结果：所有组均存在左侧化MTL激活。我们发现，成人患者的MTL激活幅度大于儿童患者，儿童对照组的MTL激活幅度大于患者。对照组的前部激活幅度更大，而患者的后部激活幅度更大。
左侧MTL的偏侧化与儿童的语言、言语和视觉记忆功能相关，左后MTL的激活强度与成人的言语记忆相关。
意义：我们的语言fMRI任务诱发了左侧化语言和MTL激活。激活与神经心理学测试之间的关系表明，这种激活与记忆功能的评估在功能上具有相关性。我们的ADDT任务可能同时支持语言
癫痫手术前的认知和记忆评估。

papers.title: Analysis of factors associated with bone loss induced by long-term antiseizure medication use and exploration of potential monitoring markers.
papers.title_zh: 长期使用抗癫痫药物所致骨质流失相关因素分析及潜在监测标志物探索。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Long-term antiseizure medication (ASM) use can lead to decreased bone mineral density (BMD) and an increased risk of fractures; however, the underlying mechanisms and key risk factors remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the impact of long-term ASM therapy on bone health in patients with epilepsy, with a specific focus on the associations of bone resorption markers, medication duration, and vitamin D status with hip and lumbar BMD, and to identify the critical time threshold for hip bone loss.
METHODS: A total of 39 patients with epilepsy receiving long-term ASM therapy were enrolled. Clinical data were collected, and serum levels of cross-linked N-telopeptide of type I collagen, cross-linked C-telopeptide of type I collagen, bone gamma-carboxyglutamic acid-containing protein, vitamin D, and other biochemical markers were measured. Vitamin D receptor-BsmI genotyping was also performed. BMD Z-scores at the hip and lumbar spine were measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Spearman rank correlation, multiple linear regression, and subgroup stratified analyses were employed to evaluate the associations among variables.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis revealed that NTX-1 levels (ρ = -0.419, p = 0.008) and the duration of ASM use (ρ = -0.361, p = 0.024) were significantly and negatively correlated with hip BMD. In the multivariate regression model, elevated NTX-1 levels were independently associated with decreased hip BMD; an independent subgroup sensitivity analysis further validated the robustness of this association (ρ = -0.4023, p = 0.0338). Stratified analysis by medication duration demonstrated that the hip BMD in the ≥ 5-year group was significantly lower than that in the < 5-year group (-1.39 vs. -0.82, p = 0.006). Neither NTX-1 levels nor medication duration showed a significant association with lumbar BMD. The mean serum vitamin D level was generally low (17.3 ± 7.1 ng/ml), and no significant correlation was observed between VDR-BsmI genotypes (84.6% bb genotype) and BMD.
CONCLUSION: Patients with epilepsy on long-term ASM therapy face a significant risk of reduced hip bone mass. Elevated serum NTX-1 levels and an ASM duration of ≥ 5 years are independent risk factors for decreased hip BMD, suggesting that the hip may be a more sensitive monitoring site for ASM-induced bone loss. Routine monitoring of hip BMD and serum NTX-1, along with proactive supplementation of vitamin D and calcium, is recommended for the early detection and intervention of drug-induced loss of bone strength.

papers.title: Direct cortical electrical stimulation-induced seizures: Are they reliable? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.title_zh: 直接皮质电刺激诱发的癫痫发作：是否可靠？系统综述和荟萃分析。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract: We aimed to assess the frequency, clinical relevance, and prognostic value of stimulation-induced seizures (SIS) during intracranial EEG recording (iEEG), and to compare high-frequency (HF) and low-frequency (LF) stimulation protocols. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting SIS during preoperative iEEG. Pooled proportions of SIS and habitual seizures were estimated using random-effects models. Differences between HF and LF stimulation were assessed using odds ratios. Study-level meta-regression was conducted to evaluate associations between SIS rates, habitual seizure proportions, and postoperative favorable seizure outcome (Engel Ia). Twenty-five studies were included. SIS occurred more frequently with HF than LF stimulation (56.1% vs. 35.8%; OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.50-2.23; p < 0.001), with substantial between-study heterogeneity. Among patients with SIS, LF stimulation was associated with a higher proportion of habitual seizures compared to HF (81.8% vs. 72.9%), although this difference was not statistically significant. A higher proportion of habitual electro-clinical seizures among SIS correlated with increased rates of favorable seizure outcomes with LF stimulation (p = 0.004) but not with HF stimulation (p = 0,912). Finally, MRI-visible lesions and the mesio-temporal seizure-onset zone were associated with higher SIS rates (p < 0.01). In conclusion, HF stimulation increases the likelihood of inducing SIS, but SIS frequency was not associated with a higher proportion of favorable seizure outcomes. Instead, the clinical relevance of SIS depends on their similarity to habitual seizures. These findings suggest that SIS may reflect underlying network excitability, and that their diagnostic value lies in their semiological and EEG concordance rather than occurrence of stimulated seizures alone. Overall, these results emphasize the importance of stimulation-induced habitual electro-clinical seizures for postsurgical outcome prognostication.

papers.title: The hidden cost of seizure suppression: Understanding neurological outcome in refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus.
papers.title_zh: 抑制癫痫发作的隐性成本：了解难治性和超难治性癫痫持续状态的神经学结局。
papers.abstract: Refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus are usually treated with continuous intravenous anesthetic drugs to achieve seizure suppression, often for days or weeks. This strategy is supported by a compelling biological rationale; prolonged seizures can promote excitotoxicity, neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and neuronal injury. Yet direct evidence that deeper or longer anesthetic coma improves long-term neurological outcome remains limited. A recurrent clinical problem is that patients who receive the most aggressive treatment are also those with the longest, most severe, and most treatment-resistant forms of status epilepticus, often in the context of high-risk underlying etiologies. Clinical complexity, seizure activity, and treatment exposure therefore become tightly intertwined. This article argues that neurological outcome after refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus should be interpreted through the interaction of three domains: the underlying disease, the epileptic process, and the burden imposed by treatment. This perspective may help explain why survivors with different etiologies, including cryptogenic new onset refractory status epilepticus, febrile infection-related epilepsy syndrome, autoimmune encephalitis, developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, metabolic disorders, and acute symptomatic conditions, may converge toward a shared long-term phenotype characterized by cognitive impairment, functional disability, persistent epilepsy, and cerebral atrophy. Current evidence does not allow the relative contribution of these domains to be quantified in individual patients. It does, however, challenge a purely seizure-centered interpretation of outcome and supports a therapeutic aim of timely seizure control with the lowest cumulative anesthetic exposure required to achieve and maintain it. Future studies should model disease, seizure, and treatment burden together using longitudinal and time-dependent variables.

papers.title: Intranasal embelin-nanostructured lipid carrier with β-cyclodextrin inclusion complex (EBCD) produces sustained behavioural control of convulsive activity in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model: A behavioural and neurochemical comparison with intranasal diazepam.
papers.title_zh: 含有β-环糊精包合络合物（EBCD）的鼻内给药紫胶素-纳米结构脂质载体在锂-匹罗卡品大鼠模型中产生对惊厥活动的持续行为控制：与鼻内给药地西泮的行为和神经化学比较。
papers.abstract: Status epilepticus (SE) is a neurological emergency requiring rapid behavioural control of convulsive activity. First-line benzodiazepines are frequently administered through delayed or invasive routes, and lose effectiveness as seizure persist. This study evaluated an intranasal embelin-β-cyclodextrin nanostructured lipid carrier (EBCD) as a behavioural proof-of-concept treatment in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model, using intranasal diazepam as reference. Treatment was withheld until continuous Racine stage 3-5 activity had been confirmed behaviourally. Seizures were scored for 60 min using modified Racine scale, and whole-tissue hippocampal GABA, glutamate, and acetylcholine quantified by LC-QTOF-MS; acetylcholine in the treated groups fell below the lowest calibrator and untreated-control glutamate exceeded the highest; both are semi-quantitative. Of 24 rats, 16 developed SE and were assigned to untreated control (n = 4), intranasal diazepam (n = 6), or intranasal EBCD (n = 6). Both treatment groups achieved sustained control of convulsive activity in all animals, whereas none of the untreated rats did (log-rank P = 0.0076). Seizure burden fell in both treated groups, significantly for diazepam versus untreated SE (adjusted P = 0.006) but not for EBCD (adjusted P = 0.10), the EBCD-diazepam difference was not significant (adjusted P = 0.83). The study was not powered as a non-inferiority comparison and does not establish equivalence. Hippocampal glutamate was elevated in untreated SE and reduced by both treatments (P = 0.014), indicating reduced glutamatergic tone, and GABA did not differ. These findings demonstrate that intranasal EBCD merits evaluation in a video-EEG-confirmed dose-response study supports its further development as a rapid nose-to-brain intranasal therapy.

papers.title: Surgical treatment of extratemporal epilepsy in children: seizure outcomes, complications and patterns of relapse.
papers.title_zh: 儿童颞外癫痫的手术治疗：癫痫发作的结局、并发症和复发模式。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extratemporal resections are increasingly performed in children with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but contemporary pediatric-only cohorts are scarce and reported seizure freedom has been modest. We examined seizure outcome, complications, and patterns of seizure recurrence in a national, population-based cohort.
METHODS: We reviewed all children (<19 years at surgery) who underwent unilobar extratemporal resection for DRE at Helsinki University Hospital, Finland's national center for pediatric epilepsy surgery, between 2003 and 2024. Seizure outcome was classified by the Engel scale at last follow-up. Freedom from seizure recurrence after the first resection was estimated with the Kaplan-Meier method, and predictors of recurrence were assessed by Cox regression.
RESULTS: Of 105 children (median follow-up 3.9 years, IQR 2.1-8.4), focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) was the most common etiology (69.5%). Engel class 1 was achieved in 58.1% overall (81.8% for long-term epilepsy-associated tumors, 65.0% for FCD type 2, 50.0% for tuberous sclerosis complex, and 35.5% for FCD type 1), and in 65.5% of children operated on from 2012 onward compared with 48.9% before 2012. Surgical complications occurred in 3.8% (permanent in 1.9%). Among children with recurrence, 55.6% recurred within 6 months, and 25.9% recurred late (≥2 years). In multivariable analysis, malformations of cortical development (HR 4.4; 95% CI 1.7-11.8), acute (HR 5.5; 95% CI 2.6-11.7) and early (HR 3.3; 95% CI 1.6-7.0) postoperative seizures, and preoperative SPECT (HR 3.0; 95% CI 1.5-6.0) were associated with recurrence, and preoperative 3T MRI with a lower risk (HR 0.3; 95% CI 0.2-0.7), whereas surgical era was not.
CONCLUSIONS: Unilobar extratemporal resection rendered most children seizure-free with few permanent deficits. Recurrence was mostly early, but a quarter of recurrences occurred after 2 years. Preoperative 3T MRI was associated with a lower risk of recurrence independently of surgical era, suggesting that improved lesion detection, rather than calendar era itself, underlies the improvement.

papers.title: Seizure-like behaviors in a mutant mouse with increased calpain-dependent cleavage of αII-spectrin.
papers.title_zh: αII-谱蛋白钙蛋白酶依赖性裂解增加的突变小鼠中癫痫样行为。
papers.abstract: Mutations inSPTAN1, the gene encoding the neuronal cytoskeletal protein αII-spectrin, are associated with epilepsy and movement disorders, complicating the clinical interpretation of seizure-like behaviors. Stress-induced paroxysmal motor events can mimic behaviors typically observed in epileptic seizures, yet they do not exhibit definitive electrophysiological correlates. This study investigated the link between seizure-like behaviors and the brain's cortical electroencephalographic (EEG) activity in heterozygousSptan1R1098Q mice, a novel model of spectrin-related neurodevelopmental disease. Mutant and wild-type (WT) mice were subject to automated gait analysis, long-term video-EEG monitoring, and a handling-induced seizure susceptibility (HISS) paradigm at various ages. R1098Q mice demonstrated pronounced gait abnormalities characteristic of ataxia as well as age-related increases in delta and theta power, and spike-wave discharges (SWD), suggesting elevated network excitability. During the HISS test, nearly all mutant mice exhibited significant seizure-like motor responses, such as forelimb clonus, impaired balance, and falls, whereas WT mice displayed no abnormal reactions. Notably, these motor behaviors did not coincide with cortical ictal EEG activity. Rather, stress induced a transient suppression of cortical EEG spiking, followed by the return of interictal spiking and SWDs. The present findings demonstrate a dissociation between seizure-like behaviors and cortical ictal EEG activity inSptan1R1098Q mice. These findings emphasize the limitations inherent to classifying seizures based solely on behavioral observations and underscore the necessity of incorporating electrophysiological data when evaluating seizure-like manifestations in genetic epilepsy models characterized by significant motor dysfunction. Such differentiation holds substantial relevance for preclinical epilepsy research and informs the interpretation of seizure-like events within neurogenetic disorders.

papers.title: Reproductive health practices and access to preconception care among women with epilepsy in Cameroon.
papers.title_zh: 喀麦隆癫痫女性的生殖健康做法和获得孕前保健的机会。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy is a critical period for women with epilepsy (WWE), which requires careful planning, preconception care, and specialized care. In many low-resource settings, access to reproductive health information and epilepsy-specific pregnancy care remains limited. This study aimed to assess knowledge, reproductive health practices, and access to preconception care among women with epilepsy in the North West of Cameroon.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of WWE who had been pregnant at least once following epilepsy diagnosis. Using a structured questionnaire, we assessed sociodemographic characteristics, epilepsy history, contraceptive use, preconception counseling, pregnancy planning, antenatal care utilization, and knowledge regarding epilepsy and pregnancy.
RESULTS: We included 100 WWE participants with a mean age of 30.6 ± 8.8 years. The total number of pregnancies after epilepsy diagnosis was 245, with a mean number of 2.45 ± 1.65. Prior to pregnancy, 86% were not receiving follow-up care for epilepsy. Preconception counseling on the effects of epilepsy on pregnancy, the effects of pregnancy on epilepsy, and pregnancy-related precautions had never been received by 88%, 92%, and 92% of participants, respectively. Sixty percent reported unplanned pregnancies, while only 4% informed a healthcare provider before conception. During pregnancy, 52% were not followed by any healthcare professional.
CONCLUSIONS: There were substantial gaps in reproductive health knowledge, preconception counseling, and specialist pregnancy care among WWE in this study. Integration of epilepsy services into reproductive and maternal healthcare programs is urgently needed.

papers.title: Barriers and facilitators to anxiety and depression treatment in epilepsy: A qualitative interview study of patient perspectives.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫患者焦虑和抑郁治疗的障碍与促进因素：一项基于患者视角的定性访谈研究。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Anxiety and depression are common in epilepsy and often undertreated, yet little is known about epilepsy patient experiences of mental health care and patient-level barriers and facilitators to mental health care. We aimed to evaluate epilepsy patient perspectives on anxiety and depression and its treatment using qualitative methods, with primary objective to assess barriers and facilitators to care for anxiety and depression.
METHODS: Participants recruited from a study examining usual care outcomes among adults with epilepsy and anxiety and/or depression symptoms completed focused semi-structured telephone interviews (NCT03879525). The interview guide explored experiences with anxiety and depression symptoms, treatment preferences, and care barriers and facilitators. Interviews were recorded, professionally transcribed and cleaned to ensure accuracy. Thematic analysis was conducted using deductive and inductive approaches. Two experts in qualitative analysis generated the codebook, coded all interviews and completed analysis using NVIVO software.
RESULTS: The study sample (N = 16) included 11 women (69%). Four participants (25%) identified as Black, one as Native American, and one as multiracial; 10 (63%) identified as white/non-Hispanic. Most participants indicated current significant impact of anxiety and/or depression on daily life, and many discussed a link between anxiety and/or depression and their epilepsy, including fear related to Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy (SUDEP). Most participants had previously engaged in treatment for anxiety and/or depression, most often medications, psychotherapy, or healthy living behaviors. Top barriers in seeking treatment for anxiety and/or depression were provider rapport/communication, transportation limitations, and individual hesitancy to seek treatment or add medication. Treatment facilitators included family, support groups, and neurologist efforts to facilitate treatment. Trust emerged as a key theme in provider interactions across various provider specialties, including neurology.
CONCLUSION: While barriers and facilitators to mental health care in epilepsy were identified at many levels for potential intervention, ranging from individual patient-level to broader societal/social factors, key actionable contributors at the neurology provider level were identified. Trust and provider rapport/communications were important drivers of mental health treatment experience, neurologists' willingness to serve as mental health provider was a key facilitator, and participants were comfortable with their neurologist acting as mental health provider.

papers.title: Epilepsy landscape in the Democratic Republic of Congo: A narrative review.
papers.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国的癫痫病现状：综述。
papers.abstract: Epilepsy is a major public health problem in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), disproportionately affecting a young population in a context of limited resources. In this narrative review, we synthesise available epilepsy data from the DRC published between 1990 and 2025. No nationwide, population-based study has been conducted, and existing data come from heterogeneous sources, mostly hospital-based or small regional surveys. The overall epilepsy prevalence is estimated to be between 0.7 % and 1.8 % nationally, representing approximately 700,000 to 1,900,000 people living with epilepsy in a population of 105-109 million. The predominant epilepsy risk factors for epilepsy in DRC include perinatal encephalopathies, central nervous system infections, particularly cerebral malaria, neurocysticercosis, onchocerciasis, meningitis, and traumatic brain injuries. Recent clinic-based data suggest that the average age of seizure onset is 13.1 years +/- 11.2 years, with a wide range spanning from 5 days, and male-to-female ratios ranging from 1.1 to 1.9. Convulsive seizures dominate the clinical picture in the available series. The therapeutic gap remains considerable, with an estimated 75-80 % of people with epilepsy lacking access to appropriate care, a situation exacerbated by persistent sociocultural stigma, a shortage of neurologists (10 per 109 million inhabitants), and the scarcity of diagnostic and monitoring facilities. These findings underscore the urgent need for national management strategies that integrate prevention of avoidable causes, decentralised diagnostic services, improved access to antiseizure medication, and sustained community awareness campaigns.

papers.title: Maternal exposure to lacosamide and zonisamide during pregnancy and risk of major congenital malformations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.title_zh: 孕期孕妇暴露于拉科沙胺和唑尼沙胺与重大先天性畸形风险：一项系统综述和荟萃分析。
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective seizure control is critical during pregnancy but established first-line antiseizure medications (ASMs) carry variable teratogenic risks, and alternative options are needed. Newer ASMs like lacosamide and zonisamide are increasingly prescribed, yet their comparative safety regarding major congenital malformations (MCMs) remains incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate and synthesize the risk of MCMs associated with maternal exposure to zonisamide or lacosamide monotherapy during pregnancy.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception to January 2026. Data on MCMs were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis of proportions for zonisamide and aggregate event rates for lacosamide.
RESULTS: Ten studies encompassing registry and observational cohorts met the inclusion criteria. The primary random effects meta-analysis of five registries with 303 patients demonstrated a pooled MCM rate for zonisamide of 1.3% (95% CI: 0.5-3.5%;I2 = 1.2%). Out of a total of 142 pregnancies exposed to lacosamide, there were zero reported cases of MCM. Thus, a conventional meta-analysis could not be performed. However, the pooled estimate based on the aggregate data was 0% (exact 95% CI 0.0-2.6%).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence on zonisamide and lacosamide in pregnancy is constrained by small numbers of exposed pregnancies and imprecise estimates. Although observed malformation rates were low, the data do not permit reliable exclusion of a clinically meaningful increase in risk. Further large, prospective registry data are required before the safety of these agents can be considered established.

papers.title: Periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs) during NREM sleep before nocturnal seizures in temporal and extratemporal lobe epilepsy: An exploratory quantitative EEG study.
papers.title_zh: 颞叶和颞外叶癫痫中夜间癫痫发作前NREM睡眠期间的周期性非癫痫样放电（PGND）：一项探索性定量EEG研究。
papers.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: To explore whether the spectral power of periodic generalized nonepileptiform discharges (PGNDs), a newly operationalized subset of CAP A-like NREM slow-wave events, differs between temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and extratemporal lobe epilepsy (ETLE), and to identify demographic, clinical, and etiological factors associated with delta power.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients undergoing long-term video-EEG monitoring (2018-2024) with at least two PGNDs in the preictal period of nocturnal seizures. PGNDs were visually scored and subtyped, and matched interictal NREM controls were selected. Absolute and relative (amplitude-normalized) spectral power was calculated for five frequency bands. Analyses were performed at the patient level, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, cross-validated ROC analysis, confounder-adjusted models, and a mixed-effects model for determinants of delta power.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients (35 TLE, 33 ETLE; 124 seizures, 711 PGNDs) met inclusion criteria. Delta (0.5-2.4 Hz) power of the PGND just before seizure onset (PGND1) was higher in ETLE than TLE, both in absolute terms (p = 0.016) and relative to total power (51.6% vs. 45.1%, p = 0.006, FDR q = 0.035), and the difference persisted after adjustment for carbamazepine use. Discrimination was modest (AUC=0.669; leave-one-out sensitivity 61%, specificity 74%). Absolute electrode-level differences did not survive FDR correction, whereas relative PGND1 delta power remained higher in ETLE at 16 of 20 electrodes after correction, indicating a widespread rather than regional difference. No within-patient preictal increase in PGND power was observed. Only febrile seizure history was independently associated with delta power.
CONCLUSIONS: PGND delta power differs between ETLE and TLE independently of overall EEG amplitude, suggesting localization-related differences in NREM slow-wave events rather than a preictal biomarker. Given the modest discrimination and exploratory design, validation in independent cohorts is required before any clinical application.

papers.title: Calibration-Free Cross-Subject SSVEP Recognition by Fusing Template-Based Transfer Learning With Transformer-Based Deep Learning.
papers.title_zh: 通过融合基于模板的迁移学习与基于Transformer的深度学习实现无校准跨受试者SSVEP识别。
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) based on steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEPs) commonly require subject-specific calibration, which limits their practical deployment for new users. This study aims to develop a calibration-free cross-subject SSVEP recognition method by integrating template-based transfer learning with Transformer-based deep learning.Approach. We propose a calibration-free cross-subject SSVEP recognition method that integrates SSVEPformer with a traditional transfer algorithm based on common impulse responses (CIRs) and transferred templates (TTs). For clarity, the complete traditional transfer algorithm is hereafter referred to as the CIR-TT algorithm, and the proposed fusion method is termed CIR-TT-SSVEPformer. For each trial, the CIR-TT algorithm generates a class-matching score vector that is introduced into SSVEPformer through two pathways. The first pathway converts the scores into channel scaling coefficients to reweight frequency-domain electroencephalographic features. The second pathway projects the scores into an auxiliary token and concatenates it with the token sequence derived from the electroencephalographic features before Transformer encoding. The method was evaluated on two public datasets and one self-collected dataset using a strict leave-one-participant-out protocol, in which the target subject was used only for testing and contributed no data to model training, transfer-prior construction, or subject-specific calibration.Main results. Across data lengths from 0.2 to 1.2 s, CIR-TT-SSVEPformer outperformed the comparison methods overall on all three datasets. At 1.2 s, the classification accuracies were 91.56%, 86.30%, and 92.69%, respectively. Ablation and mechanistic analyses showed that the two pathways can provide partially complementary contributions, while their joint effect is not strictly additive. The source-subject number and feature-visualization analyses further supported the stability of the proposed method.Significance. These findings demonstrate that fusing template-based transfer learning with Transformer-based deep learning is effective for calibration-free cross-subject SSVEP recognition and may facilitate the practical deployment of BCIs for new users.&#xD.

papers.title: BCI-FIT: Feasibility of a customization protocol for communication brain-computer interface systems.
papers.title_zh: BCI-FIT：用于通信脑机接口系统的定制协议可行性。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The BCI Functional Implementation Toolkit (BCI-FIT) is a flexible, user-centered, interdisciplinary customization protocol for non-implantable communication brain-computer interface (cBCI) systems. Here we describe the protocol and present results of a non-experimental exploratory study of the feasibility of this approach and its effects on accuracy, speed, and user experience.
APPROACH: Five participants with speech and/or physical impairments resulting from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) completed calibration and copy-spelling tasks with both customized and non-customized versions of a non-implantable cBCI over multiple visits. System customization was adjusted after each visit based on typing performance, participant preferences, clinical observations, brain signal characteristics, and results of simulations and other offline exploration.
MAIN RESULTS: Three participants demonstrated consistently high typing accuracy under both conditions, with better typing speed and/or user experience under the customized condition. Two participants had low typing accuracy that did not improve with system customization. The subset of parameters modified, and how they were modified, varied widely across participants due to their different needs and preferences. Participants with high typing accuracy reported that system customization led to improvements in comfort, workload, typing performance, and aesthetic appeal.
SIGNIFICANCE: Customization may improve cBCI typing performance and user experience for some individuals with disabilities, but additional investigation is needed. Participant preferences, clinical observations, brain-signal characteristics, simulation results, and typing performance all influenced customization decisions. Additional customization options could support successful cBCI use for a wider range of users.

papers.title: Capacity-controlled EEG denoising: diminishing reconstruction returns on semi-synthetic benchmarks and task-dependent downstream utility.
papers.title_zh: 容量受控的EEG去噪：在半合成基准和任务相关的下游效用方面，重建收益有所降低。
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) denoising is often ranked by clean-reference reconstruction metrics, although downstream task performance is less often assessed. We tested capacity effects and when reconstruction fidelity tracks utility.Approach. A depthwise-separable convolutional denoiser spanned 1.05K-40.26K parameters. Capacity was evaluated on semi-synthetic clean-reference benchmarks (EEGDenoiseNet and a mixed-artifact corpus) and by zero-shot reconstruction on brain-computer interface (BCI) Competition IV-2a/IV-2b. Downstream effects and same-condition metric-utility associations used IV-2a motor imagery, with subjects as inferential units (n=9). Further tests used an IV-2b cross-session replication and within-subject paired-recording sleep staging in 75 Sleep-EDF subjects.Main results. In these semi-synthetic reconstruction settings, capacity effects depended on metric and dataset. Electrooculographic (EOG) reconstruction improved from base8 to base16 (correlation-coefficient increment 0.007264, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.005525-0.009002), whereas electromyographic (EMG) correlation coefficient met the selected practical-saturation criterion from base6 to base8. These intervals are conditional on fixed benchmark source pools; a source-level bootstrap left both classifications unchanged. On IV-2a, matched denoising reduced common spatial patterns with linear discriminant analysis (CSP+LDA) accuracy for EOG (Δ=-0.057, 95% CI -0.087 to -0.029), EMG (-0.102, -0.152 to -0.056), and mixed contamination (-0.099, -0.152 to -0.046); these effects were supported under Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (BH-FDR) control, not Holm familywise control. ShallowFBCSPNet and EEGConformer showed reductions in several conditions, whereas EEGNet and Deep4Net had no multiplicity-corrected effects. Reconstruction metrics were associated with downstream change in some EMG/mixed conditions but not consistently for EOG. In Sleep-EDF paired-recording validation, denoisers reduced sleep-stage balanced accuracy under synthetic-EOG and unmodified-recording controls; base16 changes were -0.050 and -0.074. IV-2b effects were near-null under the evaluated 01T/02T-to-03T cross-session protocol.Significance. Reconstruction fidelity is informative but not a universal surrogate endpoint. Capacity claims from semi-synthetic benchmarks should distinguish formal practical saturation from diminishing returns, and denoising evaluation should report subject-level effects and transfer controls.

papers.title: Feasibility of Cortical Visual Neuroprostheses for Mobility in Blind Individuals.
papers.title_zh: 皮层视觉神经假体对盲人行动能力的可行性。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cortical visual neuroprostheses can provide blind individuals with perceptual information, but their effectiveness in dynamic, real-world conditions, particularly during movement, remains largely unknown. To address this gap, we examined the impact of movement on phosphene perception thresholds, whether stimulation thresholds could be derived from neural responses during mobility, and whether phosphenes could effectively support navigation in behavioural tasks.
APPROACH: Three blind volunteers were implanted with a 100-electrode Utah Electrode Array in the early occipital cortex as an interface for a cortical visual neuroprosthesis. We measured phosphene perception thresholds in sitting, standing, and walking conditions and estimated detection thresholds from concurrently recorded multi-unit activity during the threshold tasks. Additionally, mobility performance was assessed by analyzing participants' behavioral responses to cortical stimulation during controlled mobility tasks.
MAIN RESULTS: Phosphene thresholds did not differ significantly between sitting and walking, with secondary analyses including standing showing consistent results, suggesting that stimulation levels established in a seated condition may remain suitable during mobility. Neural-response-derived thresholds could also be estimated during walking, indicating that movement did not preclude threshold estimation from recorded neural activity. Across repeated navigation trials, participants increased their walking speed while successfully using phosphene cues to guide navigation, demonstrating the potential of cortical visual prostheses to support functional mobility.
SIGNIFICANCE: These findings support the reliability of intracortical microstimulation during movement and the feasibility of deriving stimulation thresholds from neural responses under dynamic conditions. This provides a foundation for future closed-loop approaches and represents an important step toward translating precision cortical stimulation from controlled laboratory settings to mobility-relevant applications.Clinical trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02983370.&#xD.

papers.title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of Alzheimer's disease through EEG normative modeling.
papers.title_zh: 通过脑电图规范建模来表征阿尔茨海默病的异质性。
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To integrate normative modeling with non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) to characterize individualized brain functional abnormalities across Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), thereby elucidating disease heterogeneity and enabling biologically informed stratification.
METHODS: We constructed sex-specific normative age models for the small-world (SW) architecture of hemispheric EEG networks and quantified individual SW deviations in 160 AD, 161 MCI, and 769 healthy controls (HCs) across multiple datasets. Individual deviation profiles were used to delineate sex-dependent topological alterations across the cognitive spectrum. We further performed unsupervised clustering to identify subtypes for both AD and MCI, and characterized their inter-subtype similarities and differences. The identified subtypes were rigorously validated for internal/external consistency and specificity.
RESULTS: EEG normative models (NMs) captured frequency-specific aging trajectories of SW organization and revealed progressive sex-related divergence in SW deviation with cognitive decline. Both MCI and AD cohorts were consistently classified into two EEG-defined subtypes with distinct intrinsic dysconnectivity patterns and cognitive profiles, despite no differences in canonical multimodal MRI measures. Subtype-1 exhibited relatively preserved network organization and distinctive neurocognitive recovery patterns, whereas subtype-2 showed widespread network disruption and poorer clinical outcomes. Cross-stage analyses demonstrated shared EEG signatures between corresponding MCI and AD subtype pairs, supporting their biological continuity. Multidimensional validation confirmed the robustness and generalizability of our subtyping framework.
CONCLUSIONS: NM-guided EEG profiling reveals clinically meaningful neurobiological heterogeneity cross the AD spectrum and identifies a high-risk MCI subtype before detectable cerebral atrophy.
SIGNIFICANCE: This framework provides an individualized, non-invasive strategy for early AD subtyping and prognostic stratification.

papers.title: Beyond the binary: excitatory rTMS of the right Broca's Homolog in Subacute Aphasia reveals a differential spectrum of individualized neuroplastic compensation.
papers.title_zh: 超越二元性：亚急性失语症患者右侧Broca区同源区的兴奋性rTMS揭示了个体化神经可塑性代偿的差异谱。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of the right hemisphere in aphasia recovery remains a central debate in neurorehabilitation. While traditional paradigms often focus on a binary "excitation vs. inhibition" logic, the dynamic nature of the subacute recovery window suggests that a more nuanced, state-dependent approach is required.
METHODS: In this study, we investigated the efficacy and neural mechanisms of high-frequency (excitatory) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) targeting the right inferior frontal gyrus in subacute post-stroke aphasia. Participants received 18 sessions of active or sham HF-rTMS over three weeks, integrated with conventional speech-language therapy. Neurophysiological evaluation was performed using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during a Verbal Fluency Task (VFT) to measure task-related hemodynamic responses (ΔHbO, ΔDHb and ΔtHb) and interhemispheric dynamics at baseline and post-intervention.
RESULTS: Active HF-rTMS yielded significantly greater gains in the Aphasia Quotient (AQ) compared to sham stimulation. Neurally, the active group exhibited a specific modulation of the right inferior frontal gyrus; however, rather than a uniform increase in excitability, we identified a "differential adaptive spectrum" consisting of both hemodynamic "increasers" and " decreasers." These heterogeneous responses correlated with distinct behavioral recovery trajectories, suggesting that the same excitatory stimulus can facilitate different compensatory pathways depending on the individual's baseline network state.
CONCLUSION: Conclusions: High-frequency stimulation of the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) may support language recovery in subacute post-stroke aphasia, but the accompanying hemodynamic responses appear to differ across individuals. These findings indicate that the functional role of the right hemisphere cannot be reduced to a uniformly maladaptive or compensatory process. Accordingly, inhibitory and excitatory stimulation of the right hemisphere may not be equally appropriate for all patients. Future studies should determine whether baseline clinical and neurophysiological profiles can be used to guide more individualized selection of stimulation polarity and target.

papers.title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for multiple sclerosis: A clinical framework for high-impact symptoms and family-centered care.
papers.title_zh: 基于神经科学的多发性硬化症心理教育：针对高影响症状和以家庭为中心的护理的临床框架。
papers.abstract: Speech and communication disorders have historically been framed as behavioral habits or peripheral motor problems, an interpretation that obscures their neurobiological complexity, contributes to stigma, and may discourage people from seeking treatment. This chapter applies the framework of Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation (NIPE) to speech disorders, focusing on developmental stuttering, childhood apraxia of speech, and Tourette syndrome with vocal tics, while drawing on obsessive-compulsive disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorder as mechanistically informative comparators. We integrate evidence suggesting that speech symptoms emerge from interactions among distributed cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical loops, cerebellar timing and prediction networks, auditory-motor integration pathways, executive and limbic systems, and glial mechanisms that regulate circuit stability. Within this framework, symptom variability and heterogeneous treatment response are reframed as expected features of state-dependent neural systems rather than failures of effort, motivation, or character. We describe how NIPE can translate these mechanisms into accessible, non-reductionist explanations that complement speech therapy, pharmacotherapy, neuromodulation, and multidisciplinary care by aligning expectations, reducing stigma, and supporting engagement during the gradual process of neuroplastic change. We also consider precision NIPE tailored to dominant mechanism profiles, the promise and ethical risks of digital delivery, and key limitations, including neurobiological oversimplification and limited direct trial evidence, that define priorities for establishing NIPE as a rigorously tested, person-centered component of care.

papers.title: When does personalization matter? An evidence-to-action beyond smart devices demonstrating the added clinical value of personalization in precision MedTech.
papers.title_zh: 个性化在何时至关重要？超越智能设备的“证据到行动”实践，展示个性化在精准医疗技术中的临床附加价值。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Precision medicine (PM) seeks to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment by incorporating biologic, clinical, environmental, and behavioral variation rather than relying exclusively on population averages. Medical technology (MedTech) provides a practical interface through which this approach can be translated into continuous sensing, decision support, and individualized intervention. We use the term personalized/precision medical devices (PMDs) for a conceptual class of devices that combine person-specific inputs with analytics and device-level configuration or adaptation. PMDs overlap with smart devices, connected health, and digital therapeutics, but are distinguished by their explicit coupling of individualized data to clinically meaningful device behavior.
METHODS: This perspective uses a structured narrative literature approach. The literature survey was extended through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and major regulatory/standards sources for publications addressing precision or personalized medicine, biosensing, wearable and implantable devices, point-of-care diagnostics, automated drug delivery, digital therapeutics, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), interoperability, regulation, cybersecurity, and health equity [Oct. 2025-Oct. 2026]. Preference was given to peer-reviewed clinical studies, systematic reviews, authoritative regulatory guidance, and international standards. Evidence was synthesized narratively around a device lifecycle framework linking individual profile, sensing, data infrastructure, analytics, actuation, clinical workflow, evidence generation, and governance.
RESULTS: Clinical evidence demonstrates that some components of the PMD concept are already established. In a randomized trial, automated insulin delivery increased time in the target glucose range by 14% points versus sensor-augmented pump therapy at 24 weeks. Remote pulmonary-artery pressure monitoring reduced heart-failure hospitalization by 28% in a prespecified analysis of patients with reduced ejection fraction. In the Apple Heart Study, 419,297 participants were enrolled; 0.52% received an irregular-pulse notification, and atrial fibrillation was identified in 34% of participants who returned an analyzable electrocardiographic patch. Digital therapeutics and adaptive neurostimulation further illustrate how software and implantable systems can individualize treatment, although clinical generalizability and long-term evidence remain uneven.
CONCLUSIONS: PMDs should be viewed as an engineering and clinical integration paradigm, not as a new regulatory category. Their value depends less on novelty of individual components than on reliable linkage among person-specific data, clinically validated algorithms, device actuation, and longitudinal feedback. Translation therefore requires evidence generation, interoperability, cybersecurity, lifecycle regulation, accountable AI, and equity-by-design. The next phase of precision MedTech will be defined by selective deployment of these capabilities where individualized sensing and adaptation demonstrably improve clinical outcomes or care efficiency.

papers.title: Bioiontronics: the next-generation platform for biotic-abiotic communication.
papers.title_zh: 生物离子电子学：下一代生物-非生物通信平台。
papers.abstract: Bidirectional communication between biological systems and artificial devices is a central goal of bioengineering. However, a fundamental challenge arises from the distinct signal carriers employed by these systems, as artificial devices predominantly rely on electrons, whereas biological systems communicate through ions and molecules. Bioiontronics offers a promising approach to bridge this divide by harnessing ionic and molecular transport to sense physiological signals and modulate biological functions. In this review, we examine the fundamental mechanisms underlying bioiontronic technologies, including ion-selective transport, thermogalvanic and piezoionic transduction, organic electronic ion pumps (OEIPs), electroosmotic delivery, and electrically triggered release. We discuss emerging applications in electrophysiological and pressure sensing, neuromodulation, wound healing, and drug delivery, while critically evaluating advances demonstrated in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo. We further discuss key challenges associated with ionic and molecular selectivity, constraints on the size and charge of deliverable molecules, long-term operational stability and system-level integration. By coupling electrical, chemical, and thermodynamic processes, bioiontronics holds promise for developing miniaturized, multifunctional biointerfaces that integrate sensing, information processing and actuation, ultimately enabling closed-loop communication between biological and artificial systems.

papers.title: Feedback as automatic dose selection in a basal ganglia-thalamocortical model of adaptive deep brain stimulation.
papers.title_zh: 在适应性深部脑刺激的基底神经节-丘脑皮质模型中，反馈作为自动剂量选择。
papers.abstract: We separate the effects of feedback and of stimulation dose in adaptive deep brain stimulation (DBS), using a seven-population firing-rate model of the basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop. A closed-loop advantage may reflect dose rather than feedback. The model has dopamine-dependent gains, delays, a prescribed 20-Hz beta input, and a suppressive input to the subthalamic nucleus set by a saturated proportional-integral (PI) controller on thalamic output. Dose is the command amplitude, and four constant commands are matched to the closed loop on late command, cumulative command, stimulation use, and full-horizon error. An exact window identity for integral action and a convexity condition, under which a constant command is quasi-statically at least as efficient as any time-varying command within the convex range at a fixed state, define when an advantage reflects dose. At five dopamine levels and three horizons, a constant command with equal stimulation use had lower full-horizon error than the closed loop in all 15 comparisons, and the closed loop settled within 0.004 of the constant command required. In a 200-subject cohort varying 20 parameters, including time constants and delays, the individually optimized constant command had lower error than feedback at a fixed state in all 200 subjects. After dopamine fell and recovered, the closed loop had lower error than the best constant after the change in 185, and over whole runs including its start-up, than the best constant for the schedule in 96. In this model, feedback acts as automatic dose selection whose benefit appears when the disease state changes.

papers.title: Epistemic Challenges in the Interpretation of Brain Data: A Roadmap for Aligning Divergent Inferences.
papers.title_zh: 脑数据解释中的认识论挑战：协调不同推论的路线图。
papers.abstract: Advances in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and artificial intelligence enable the identification of neural signatures-patterns of brain activity linked to thoughts, emotions, and mental states. Next-generation BCIs, including adaptive deep brain stimulation, promise personalized treatment for movement and psychiatric conditions. However, their effectiveness depends on whether neural signatures accurately reflect individuals' experiences and clinical states. Because neural signatures are abstract, they require meaningful correlations with behavior, symptoms, and clinical outcomes. Ethical challenges arise when brain data, behavioral observations, and patient self-reports conflict, raising questions about whose knowledge matters and how to determine clinical "ground truth." We argue that neural signature research needs epistemic duty-the responsibility to make well-reasoned decisions using the best available evidence-and propose three strategies to address these challenges: contextual, dimensional approaches to integrate diverse data; involving patients in decisions about data use; and stress-testing neural models to assess their robustness under uncertainty and conflicting evidence.

papers.title: Electrode-Based Neuromodulation for Refractory Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence and Clinical Integration.
papers.title_zh: 基于电极的神经调节治疗难治性疼痛性糖尿病性周围神经病变：对当前证据和临床整合的综述。
papers.abstract:
CONTEXT: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is a complex, progressive complication characterized by small-fiber degeneration, microvascular insufficiency, metabolic stress, and maladaptive central sensitization. First-line medications are generally only partially effective and frequently provide incomplete or insufficiently durable relief, underscoring the importance of mechanism-based interventions.
EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: This narrative review was based on searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from database inception through 2026, with priority given to English-language studies involving human subjects. The evidence was narratively synthesized and appraised by experts rather than systematically pooled, and no meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Neuromodulation directly modulates dysfunctional nociceptive circuits through approaches such as peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS), dorsal root ganglion stimulation (DRGS), and spinal cord stimulation (SCS). These emerging treatments may also provide microvascular and neuroimmune benefits. High-frequency and burst SCS provide nonparesthetic analgesia through mechanisms more congruent with endogenous pain-modulatory physiology, whereas closed-loop SCS based on evoked compound action potentials (ECAPs) enables real-time, stable engagement of neural tissue. Recent improvements in wireless platforms, miniaturized micro-electrode systems, and regenerative stimulation have increased therapeutic applications and decreased procedural burden while improving neural selectivity. Neuromodulation is progressing toward personalized, adaptive treatment through data-driven optimization of stimulation parameters and phenotype-specific programming, facilitated by artificial intelligence (AI). Biomarker-guided patient selection using quantitative sensory testing, intra-epidermal nerve fiber density, electrophysiologic measures, and advanced imaging is proposed as a framework for aligning therapeutic modality with disease phenotype. However, no biomarker has yet been validated to predict response to neuromodulation in PDPN, and this stratification remains hypothesis-generating and has not been prospectively validated.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuromodulation is emerging as a mechanism-targeted and increasingly individualized approach for refractory PDPN that can provide sustained pain relief and functional benefits when other treatments have been ineffective. Preliminary evidence also suggests possible disease-modifying properties, although these require confirmation in PDPN-specific, long-term comparative trials.
